extra.message: Server-side template injection via fragment parameter — Arbitrary code execution / full server compromise via Jinja2 sandbox escape gadgets [verified: fragment GET param is string-concatenated into Jinja2 Template() source and rendered, enabling SSTI/RCE via template syntax.]

OS command injection via host parameter — Arbitrary OS command execution on the server as the application user [verified: host from GET is concatenated directly into a shell string passed to os.system with no sanitization; only gate is the static ops token.]
OS command injection via host parameter — Arbitrary OS command execution on the server as the app user [verified: Duplicate of idx 0; confirmed same os.system command injection via host.]

SSRF blocklist bypass via HTTP redirect in webhook delivery — Even a webhook URL passing creation-time hostname checks can redirect the delivery worker to an internal address, fully bypassing the SSRF mitigation and reaching internal services/cloud metadata. [verified: clean_target_url in apikeys/views.py only blocklists hostnames at creation time; deliver_webhooks.py:80 calls urllib.request.urlopen directly, which follows 3xx redirects by default with no custom redirect handler, so a delivery-time 302 to an internal/metadata address bypasses the check entirely.]

SSRF via webhook target_url — incomplete blocklist allows internal/metadata targets — Attacker (any instructor/TA/school-admin) can make the server issue requests to internal-only services or the cloud metadata endpoint and read the response back via the stored WebhookDelivery.response_body, enabling internal network reconnaissance or credential theft from metadata services. [verified: Same root cause: the blocklist in WebhookForm.clean_target_url (apikeys/views.py:43-58) is a literal string match with no IP-range or DNS-resolution check, so any staff/instructor can point webhooks at internal IPs or the cloud metadata endpoint and read the response via stored WebhookDelivery records.]

Sensitive PII/secret exposure via ops endpoints — Disclosure of SSNs, card numbers, and partner sync tokens to anyone possessing the shared static ops token [verified: Endpoints return/store SSNs, card numbers, and a live-looking sync token in plaintext, gated only by a static shared header token rather than per-user auth.]

Path traversal arbitrary file write via ref parameter — Arbitrary file write/overwrite outside the export directory, potentially planting files elsewhere on disk [verified: Duplicate of idx 3; confirmed ref-based path traversal write.]

Path traversal / arbitrary file write via name parameter — Arbitrary file write on the server filesystem, potentially leading to RCE (e.g. overwriting application code or cron scripts) [verified: Duplicate of idx 18; confirmed name-based path traversal write in course_dock_shelf_389.]
XXE in XML ingestion endpoint — Local file disclosure, SSRF, and potential DoS via external entity expansion [verified: Duplicate of idx 2; confirmed same XXE-enabled parser configuration.]

No rate limiting on login and password-reset endpoints — Unlimited automated password guessing / credential stuffing against user accounts, and ability to spam password-reset emails to any address. [verified: login_view and password_reset_request use plain Django auth/email flows with no throttling middleware, django-axes, or django-ratelimit anywhere in the project, confirming absent brute-force protection on a reachable unauthenticated endpoint.]

Unrestricted role assignment in bulk user CSV import — A CSV import (already gated to school_admin) can be used to create arbitrary school_admin accounts if the uploaded file is sourced from a less-trusted party (e.g. HR spreadsheet, shared drive) — the admin performing the import may not notice a smuggled admin row among hundreds of legitimate ones. [verified: import_users_csv only validates role against Role.values (courses/views.py:441) with no restriction excluding school_admin, so a CSV row can set role=school_admin on get_or_create/update (lines 445-457), letting a bulk import mint or promote arbitrary admin accounts.]

Weak static-secret authentication for ops endpoints (timing-unsafe comparison, no rate limiting) — Facilitates brute-forcing/timing attack against the single token that gates all critical ops endpoints including RCE and XXE sinks [verified: _wrk_gate compares the token with plain `==` (not hmac.compare_digest) and is the sole, unrated-limited gate protecting every RCE/XXE/file-write sink in this file.]

Reflected XSS via copyline parameter — Script execution in the browser of anyone who can be induced to load the crafted URL (session/token theft, given credentials are shared header-based here it also risks token exfiltration if reused in a browser context) [verified: Duplicate of idx 10; confirmed unescaped copyline reflected as HTML.]

Mass assignment via unrestricted JSON merge — Demonstrates unrestricted-key overwrite pattern (e.g. setting is_admin/role/credit_limit) with no field allow-listing [verified: Raw parsed JSON body (change_set) is merged via workset.update() into a dict containing role/is_admin/credit_limit with no key allow-list, then returned.]

Sensitive data (bearer tokens) written to logs — Bearer tokens and request payloads are exposed to anyone with log access, enabling credential theft [verified: logger.warning logs the full raw request body and Authorization header verbatim at WARNING level, persisting bearer tokens into logs.]

Missing authentication on ops endpoint — Unauthenticated attackers can invoke this internal ops endpoint, inconsistent with the rest of the internal-token-gated surface [verified: course_identity_ping_334 (line 93) is the only handler lacking the `if not _wrk_gate(request): return _nope()` check present in every sibling function, making it fully unauthenticated.]

Missing authorization check on ops endpoint — Unauthenticated access to an operational endpoint that all other endpoints in the module intentionally gate [verified: Duplicate of idx 8; confirmed missing _wrk_gate call.]

CORS misconfiguration reflecting Origin with credentials allowed — Any malicious website can make credentialed requests to this endpoint and read responses, bypassing same-origin policy [verified: Origin header is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin alongside Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, allowing any origin credentialed access.]

Disabled TLS certificate verification on outbound request — Man-in-the-middle attackers can intercept/tamper with the outbound partner status request [verified: ssl._create_unverified_context() is used for the outbound urlopen call, disabling certificate validation entirely.]

Privilege escalation via client-controlled badge cookie/header — Any caller who can pass the internal ops gate can trivially set a cookie/header to obtain elevated payroll/casework data [verified: Elevated payroll/casework data is granted purely by a client-supplied cookie/header equal to 'lead' with no server-side signature or role verification beyond the shared ops token.]

CSV formula injection via student email in grade export — Formula/DDE injection leading to code execution or data exfiltration in the admin's spreadsheet application when opening the exported grades CSV [verified: s.student.email is written raw into a CSV cell at courses/views.py:554 with no leading-character sanitization; Django's EmailValidator permits local parts starting with characters like '+' or containing '=', so a self-registered student email can carry a formula payload opened later by an admin.]

CSV formula injection via student email in submissions export — Formula/DDE injection leading to code execution or data exfiltration in the admin's spreadsheet application when opening the exported submissions CSV [verified: Identical unsanitized email-to-CSV-cell pattern at courses/views.py:573, same as the already-confirmed instance at line 602 in this file.]

CSV formula/DDE injection via unsanitized student email in grade/submission/progress exports — A student can craft their registration email as a spreadsheet formula; when a school admin exports and opens grades.csv, submissions.csv, or progress.csv, the formula executes in their spreadsheet application, potentially exfiltrating local data or achieving code execution via legacy DDE payloads. [verified: csv.writer writes raw email strings with no leading-character escaping, and EmailField accepts local-parts starting with '=', '+', '-', '@' so a self-registered student email can carry a formula that executes when an admin opens the export in Excel/Sheets.]

Open redirect via lane parameter — Can be used in phishing to redirect users from a trusted domain to attacker-controlled sites [verified: lane is passed directly to django's redirect() with no allow-list/relative-path check, enabling open redirect.]

Weak cryptographic hash (MD5) used for digest — Digest values are trivially reversible/collidable, undermining any integrity or verification use of this value [verified: Unsalted MD5 is used for a phrase digest with no stated non-security use, a weak-crypto pattern reachable via GET/POST.]
Brute-forceable static PIN authentication — Attacker brute-forces the 4-digit verifier to pass this identity check [verified: Duplicate of idx 12; confirmed brute-forceable static PIN.]

Insecure PRNG used for security code generation — Predictable codes/nonces can be guessed or reproduced by an attacker who observes PRNG state [verified: random.choice (non-CSPRNG) is used to generate a 'code' value presented as a security token, making it predictable given PRNG state.]
